top_story.headline: Postal Regulatory Commission nominee Jeffrey Zisk pledges to divest FedEx, Walmart and private funds
top_story.dek: His ethics agreement also requires resigning from the Prostate Cancer Foundation and trustee posts.
paragraphs: Jeffrey Zisk, nominated as Commissioner of the Postal Regulatory Commission, submitted an ethics agreement committing to divest, within 90 days of confirmation, from Cart.com, Inc., Surrey Ventures LLC, Capisco LLC, FedEx Corp, Walmart Inc., and two private funds. The agreement also keeps certain entity interests passive-only during his tenure.

Separately, the Deadline Watch and Ethics Agreement Tracker sections below show two sitting members with no CY2025 annual disclosure on file past every extension, and seven confirmed officials with no posted compliance certification more than 30 days past deadline.

sections.headline: Zisk commits to extensive divestitures for Postal Regulatory Commission appointment
paragraphs: Three new ethics filings were submitted on October 7, including agreements and compliance certifications for presidential appointees. The documents confirm executive-branch ethics commitments including asset divestitures, position resignations, and financial recusals designed to prevent conflicts of interest.

items: Jeffrey Zisk, nominated as Commissioner of the Postal Regulatory Commission, submitted an Ethics Agreement committing to divest from Cart.com, Inc., Surrey Ventures LLC, Capisco LLC, FedEx Corp, Walmart Inc., and two private investment funds (CIC V and Apollo Accord+ II Fund, L.P.) within 90 days of confirmation. The agreement also requires resignation from his position with the Prostate Cancer Foundation and from trustee posts, while maintaining passive-only interests in certain entities during his tenure.

Preston W. Griffith, U.S. Representative to the Vienna Office of the United Nations and U.S. Representative to the International Atomic Energy Agency at the Department of State, submitted a Certification of Ethics Agreement Compliance dated September 23, 2026, confirming completion of all required resignations, divestitures, and ethics agreement obligations as of his August 7 confirmation.

William Makaneole, Ambassador to Turkmenistan at the Department of State, submitted an Ethics Agreement that includes a recusal from matters involving the University of Kentucky, where his spouse is employed, along with standard ethics commitments regarding financial interests and conflicts of interest.

sections.headline: No new stock-trade reports; three Senate annual and candidate filings land
paragraphs: No House or Senate Periodic Transaction Reports (STOCK Act trades) surfaced that hadn't already been reported in a prior edition, so no trade tables appear today. Three new Senate filings were read in full; each is listed below.

items: Sen. Tim Scott filed an amended calendar-2025 annual report on October 6. It lists $94,563 in royalties from HarperCollins Publishing LLC, $4,685 from the South Carolina Retirement System, spousal wages from MEB LLC, and a 50% interest in Rivertown Investments, LLC, which holds three South Carolina residential rentals each valued at $100,001–$250,000.

Troy D. Jackson, a candidate with state of candidacy Maine (candidacy commenced July 9, 2026), filed a candidate report on October 5. It lists $90,000 from the International Association of Machinists (paid to him and his firm, Jackson Associates) and $48,000 from the International Union of Painters and Allied Trades, plus smaller self-employment income; assets include a spousal Maine Public Employees Retirement System pension valued at $100,001–$250,000 and a Maine commercial property valued at $15,001–$50,000.

Justin Murphy, a New Jersey candidate (candidacy commenced January 15, 2026), filed a candidate report on October 7. It lists $28,500 in self-employment income as a solo attorney, no reportable assets, and a $100,001–$250,000 law-school student loan from Navient and Nel Net.

sections.headline: 16 new lobbying registrations in a day dominated by third-quarter reports
paragraphs: The Senate lobbying database posted 347 filings since October 6: 16 new registrations, 246 third-quarter activity reports (plus 46 third-quarter amendments), and a few dozen terminations and other amendments. The registrations are mostly routine; the table below lists all 16, each linked to its filing. Notable terminations include I Street Advocates ending work for the American Postal Workers Union and the National Rural Letter Carriers Association, and Holland & Knight LLP ending work for the Interactive Advertising Bureau, Inc. blocks.text: Tracking 483 Senate-confirmed officials with ethics agreements since Jan. 20, 2025. Deadlines are counted from the confirmation date on congress.gov plus the agreement's stated window (usually 90 days) -- OGE can grant extensions that aren't public, so treat each flag as a lead to confirm, not a finding. OGE posts certifications with a lag, so nothing inside 30 days of a deadline is flagged. A certification filed but not yet posted by OGE will read as missing: confirm with the agency before publishing.

sections.headline: Rep. Michael T. McCaul filed 13 trade reports last year, none in 91 days
paragraphs: 1 House member(s) with a history of frequent stock trading have stopped filing trade reports.

items: Rep. Michael T. McCaul (R-TX-10) filed 13 periodic transaction reports in the 12 months from 7/9/2025 to 7/9/2026, and none in the 91 days since the last, on 7/8/2026

blocks.text: House members who filed 6 or more periodic transaction reports (STOCK Act trade disclosures) in the year before the last 90 days and none since, per the House Clerk's disclosure index. Silence doesn't say why: the member may have sold off holdings, moved assets into a blind trust or index fund, been covered by a new law, or just not traded -- and trades are reportable up to 45 days late, so the latest ones may not be filed yet. House members only; the Senate's e-filing search isn't covered.
